name: Chronicle Map
tagline: Off-heap, memory-mapped key-value store for Java with microsecond latency and cross-process sharing.
description: Chronicle Map is an open-source Java key-value store from Chronicle Software (the OpenHFT project) that implements ConcurrentMap but keeps entries off the JVM heap in memory-mapped files. Maps can therefore hold far more data than the heap, survive restarts when backed by a file, and be shared by several JVM processes on the same host, with microsecond-level reads and writes and almost no garbage-collection pressure. You size a map up front (expected entries and average key/value size), and lookups are by key only. It is used mainly in trading and other latency-sensitive financial systems. Cross-host multi-master replication is part of Chronicle's commercial offering, and the company's product pages now lead with a Chronicle Queue-backed map, but the Apache 2.0 library keeps shipping releases (2026.1 in January 2026).

pricing.notes: Core library is Apache 2.0; replication, enterprise features and support are commercial.

scale.notes: Capacity is bounded by disk rather than heap; the open-source edition is single-host (multi-process). Cross-host replication needs the commercial edition.

strengths: Microsecond-level reads and writes with near-zero GC because data lives off-heap
Memory-mapped files let several JVMs on one host share the same map
Capacity bounded by disk rather than heap size
Apache 2.0 core with a commercial support path
weaknesses: Key lookups only: no query language or secondary indexes
Maps must be sized up front (entry count, average key and value size)
useCases: Low-latency reference data and order-book state in trading systems
Sharing state between JVM processes on one host
Large off-heap caches that survive restarts
notIdealFor: Multi-node storage without a commercial license
